insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (varies by plan; e.g., Optima Secure: 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200 Lakhs as per Annexure C)

great.name: Room Rent (No capping / At Actuals)
great.quote: Room rent limit shall be ‘At Actuals’ unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: By default, the policy covers room rent at actuals (no predefined room category limit). Some plans like Optima Select/Optima Lite may have different room limits if specified in the schedule.

great.name: Built-in Additional Sum Insured buffer (Secure Benefit) – activates after Base SI is exhausted
great.quote: The Secure Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: Extra insurer-provided Sum Insured becomes available after base SI finishes (helps in large claims). Amount depends on the plan/policy schedule.

great.name: Restore Benefit (same illness covered) – Automatic Restore Benefit
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
great.explanation: Restored SI can be used for the same illness (best-in-class restore). Frequency is once per year unless schedule says 'Unlimited Times'.

great.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus (non-resetting) – Plus Benefit irrespective of claims (if in force)
great.quote: This Cover will be applied irrespective of number of claims made under the expiring Policy.
great.explanation: If Plus Benefit is in force, SI increases on renewal even if you claim—this is stronger than typical NCB which often reduces/resets on claims.

great.name: Secure Benefit + Restore stacking order defined
great.quote: The sequence of utilization of Sum Insured in this Policy will be as follows... b. Base Sum Insured. c. Cumulative Bonus/Plus Benefit d. Secure Benefit e. Automatic Restore Benefit
great.reference: Section D – 1.19 Utilization of Sum Insured (Page 39)
great.explanation: Clear rules on how different buffers (Plus/CB, Secure Benefit, Restore) are consumed, reducing ambiguity during claims.

great.name: Optional PED waiting period reduction to 12 months or 24 months (channel-level option)
great.quote: Modification of PED waiting period from 36 months... to 24 months (2 years)... to 12 months (1 year)
great.reference: Section B.2.12 – PED waiting period modification (Page 25)
great.explanation: If this option is applied (at inception via channel), PED waiting can be as low as 12 months, which is best-in-class.

great.name: Air Ambulance covered (optional cover; limits per schedule)
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify expenses incurred... towards Ambulance transportation in an airplane or helicopter for Emergency Care...
great.explanation: Air ambulance is covered if opted/in force (limit as per policy schedule). This is a valuable benefit for emergencies.

good.name: PED Waiting Period (default)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage...
good.explanation: 36 months PED waiting is within normal/acceptable market range (not a red flag).

good.name: Specific Illness / Procedure Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.reference: Section C.1(b)(i) – Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period (Page 28-29)
good.explanation: 24 months specific disease waiting is standard in the market.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...
good.explanation: 30-day initial waiting is standard for indemnity health policies.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
good.explanation: 60 days pre-hospitalization is standard-good (some plans like Optima Lite have 30 days as per schedule).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: 180 days post-hospitalization is good/standard. (Optima Lite can be 60 days as per schedule.)

good.name: Optional cover: Protect Benefit (Non-medical expenses / consumables-like items as per annexure) if in force
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Insured Person for the Non-Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B to this Policy incurred in relation to a claim admissible under Section B -1 (Base Coverage)...
good.explanation: This is an optional upgrade that can reduce out-of-pocket non-medical items (as per Annexure B) if you opt it.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (by default) – out-of-pocket items as per Non-medical list; full cover only if Protect Benefit is in force
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as... Full list of Non -Medical Expenses is attached as ANNEXURE B... (Annexure B includes items such as) "GLOVES" ... "MASK" ... "NEBULISATION KIT" ...
bad.reference: Section C.3(k) – Specific Exclusions (Page 32) + Annexure B (Pages 49-50)
bad.explanation: By default, many consumable/non-medical items are excluded and become out-of-pocket unless you have opted Protect Benefit (which indemnifies Annexure B items for admissible claims).

bad.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus missing for this plan (Cumulative Bonus not available in Optima Secure plan chart)
bad.quote: Cumulative Bonus (CB) [Applicable to ‘Optima Suraksha’, ‘Optima Lite’ and ‘Optima Select’ plans]
bad.explanation: As per wording, CB is not applicable to all plans. If your plan variant does not include CB (e.g., Optima Secure per Annexure C shows CB as Not Covered), Sum Insured may not grow via CB.

bad.name: Restore Benefit absent if not in force (mandatory reporting; applies if your policy schedule does not include Automatic Restore Benefit)
bad.quote: The company shall instantly add 100% of the Base Sum Insured under this benefit... (Automatic Restore Benefit is an optional cover and is applicable... only if it is specified in the Policy Schedule to be in force for that Insured Person...)
bad.reference: Section B.2 – Optional Covers intro (Page 14) + Section B.2.6 (Page 17-18)
bad.explanation: Restore is a major feature. If your policy schedule/plan variant does not have Automatic Restore Benefit in force, then there is no replenishment of Sum Insured after a claim.

unclear.name: Co-pay (not explicitly stated)
unclear.quote: Def. 8. Co-Payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
unclear.explanation: The document defines co-pay but does not clearly state whether any co-pay applies by default for this plan/age. Verify co-pay (if any) in the Policy Schedule.
